title: Quarter-ring curved cantilever: plane-stress continuum oracle for the curved-beam closed form

gates.quantity: continuum limit / closed form - 1, t/R=0.05 delta_tangent
gates.reference: (3 pi/4 - 2) P R^3/(E I) + pi P R/(4 E A) + pi P R/(4 k G A)

gates.quantity: continuum limit / closed form - 1, t/R=0.05 delta_radial
gates.reference: P R^3/(2 E I) (Maxwell-Betti reciprocity with the radial load case)

gates.quantity: minimum observed convergence order over the t/R ladder
gates.reference: 2 (Q8 displacement convergence, Richardson from three nested meshes)

gates.quantity: max relative reaction residual over the ladder
gates.reference: sum(reactions) = -applied load; reaction moment = P R

gates.quantity: max inner/outer fibre |FE/Winkler-Bach - 1| over the t/R ladder
gates.reference: curved-beam hoop stress N/A + M (r - r_n)/(A e r)
declared 3 % usability envelope of the curved-beam closed form
declared 9 % penalty that a flat-beam check under-reports

limitations: Plane-stress idealisation: no out-of-plane (width-direction) stress; valid for b >> t, which the declared b/t >= 4 respects.

Flat-beam/Winkler-Bach profiles use statics-derived section resultants (N, M), so the comparison grades the stress *distribution* of the continuum solution, not an independently solved stress boundary-value problem.

The 2 % section gate excludes points within one sample of the neutral surface, where the hoop stress passes through zero and a relative deviation is meaningless; the fibre (inner/outer) gate is the graded one.
Continuum drift for t/R < 0.10 is below the extrapolation resolution, so the drift exponent is fitted on t/R >= 0.10 only.
